newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ford-Werke says 5-month sales, output down.
newsitem.headline: Ford-Werke says 5-month sales, output down.

text.p: Ford-Werke AG, the German unit of U.S. carmaker Ford Motor Co, said on Wednesday its vehicle sales for the first five months of 1997 fell about five percent to 11.1 billion marks due to weak consumer demand.
Ford said its sales from January to May fell 9.5 percent to 456,700 units, while production slumped 12 percent to 394,500 vehicles.
Ford, which exports 65 percent of the cars it makes in Germany, said the sales data reflects the sale of German-made Ford vehicles around the world.

Despite the lower sales, Ford-Werke chief executive William Boddie told the carmaker's annual general meeting that the carmaker had so far in 1997 cut costs by three percent of sales as part of a plan to return the German unit to profitabilty.
But Boddie said it would be difficult for Ford to match the same sales level in 1996 when the carmaker had sales of 26.4 billion marks and reported a loss of 551.6 million marks.
He also declined to predict when Ford-Werke would return to profitability.
"The difficult external conditions could mean that our major internal cost-cutting measures may not be reflected to the desired extent in our profit situation," Boddie said.

Ford, like other European carmakers, said it was facing difficult sales conditions in Germany due to weak consumer demand and predicted a drop of about 100,000 vehicles in 1997 German vehicle sales to about 3.3 million units.

Boddie, predicting the carmaker would have a German market share of 11.2 percent in the first half of 1997, said Ford would seek to maintain its 1996 market share level of 11.3 percent for the entire year despite prospects for sales to be below the 1.11 million vehicles sold by Ford last year.
Ford is seeking to turn around its sales outlook in part through the introduction in October of the Puma sport coupe.
